questions.q: What did Rosenthal's classroom study show?
a: Students whose teacher expected them to excel did better
Students in smaller classes always learned faster
Average students could not improve their grades
Teacher experience mattered more than expectations
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes a study where teachers told their class was gifted, and those average students ended a grade ahead.

questions.q: What is the first step in goal-setting, according to the summary?
a: Getting specific about exactly what you want
Telling everyone about your plans
Waiting for the right moment to begin
Setting a goal you know you can reach
questions.why: Lesson 2 says vague aims like being healthy go nowhere, so you should quantify what you want to change.

questions.q: What should you do after setting a goal and a timeline?
a: Break it into daily or weekly steps
Keep it private so no one can judge you
Revise it whenever progress slows
Focus on several goals at once
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to identify the small daily or weekly actions that move you toward the goal.

questions.q: What is stinkin' thinkin' in the summary?
a: A bad attitude that holds you back
A fear of speaking in public
A habit of over-planning everything
A refusal to accept praise
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses the phrase for the unproductive thinking patterns that drag all of us down.

questions.q: What does the Harvard study cited in the summary say about attitude?
a: It accounts for 85 percent of what you accomplish
It matters far less than intelligence at work
It cannot be changed after childhood
It explains only 15 percent of success
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites the finding that attitude drives 85 percent of accomplishment and intelligence only 15 percent.
